draft.title: Leaders of the new state
card: Leader of the Bolsheviks and head of the new government. He set its main policies, including the decrees, the peace and later the New Economic Policy.
A leading Bolshevik who organised the Red Army. He built it into a disciplined force that fought the Civil War.
Head of the Cheka, the secret police set up in December 1917. It used arrests and terror to crush opposition to Bolshevik rule.
A Bolshevik who became a commissar for social welfare. She pushed for women's rights, such as easier divorce and support for mothers.
draft.remember: Each leader shaped the new state in a different area: government, army, security and women's rights.

a.q: Which leader was in charge of the Cheka, the Bolshevik secret police?
a.why: Dzerzhinsky headed the Cheka, which crushed opposition to Bolshevik rule. Trotsky is the tempting answer, but he organised the Red Army, not the secret police.
a.clue: This person's name is linked to the Cheka on the card.

b.q: A new law in 1918 makes divorce easier and gives more support to mothers. Which leader is most linked with this kind of change?
b.why: Kollontai worked for women's rights as a commissar for social welfare. Lenin led the government overall, but the card links this area of reform to her.
b.clue: Which leader worked on women's rights?

check.summary: No problems found. The facts about Lenin, Trotsky, Dzerzhinsky (Cheka, December 1917) and Kollontai (commissar for social welfare) are accurate, and both questions have one clear right answer.
